title: Meeting Rooms III
summary: Process meetings in increasing original start time.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–100 rooms numbered 0 through n−1. 1–100000 rows [start,end] with 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 500000 and distinct start times. An ending meeting releases its room immediately. Delayed times may exceed signed 32-bit range.
contractDetails.output-checking: Use at least 64-bit or exact numeric time for delayed meetings. Preserve durations, select the lowest eligible room, and compare the exact usage winner.

statement: Process meetings in increasing original start time. Use the lowest-numbered room free at that time. If every room is busy, delay the meeting until the first room becomes free and preserve its duration. Break simultaneous room availability ties by room number. Return the room that hosts the most meetings, choosing the smallest number on a tie.

examples.explanation: Room 1 hosts the second, delayed third, and fourth meetings.
The equal-time release is broken by room number, and the final usage counts tie.
Original start times determine processing order, and room 0 can be reused at time 2.

constraints: 1–100 rooms numbered 0 through n−1. 1–100000 rows [start,end] with 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 500000 and distinct start times. An ending meeting releases its room immediately. Delayed times may exceed signed 32-bit range.
hints: Conceptual: The smallest free room and the earliest future release are different priorities.
Directional: Use a room-number heap for free rooms and an end-time heap for occupied rooms.
Implementation: Release every room ending at or before the requested start. If no room is free, pop the earliest ending room and schedule the same duration after its release.

expectedComplexity.time: O(m log m + m log n)
expectedComplexity.space: O(m log m + m log n)

complexityAnalysis: O(m log m + m log n) time and O(m+n) auxiliary space for m meetings and n rooms.
